title: HStencil: Matrix-Vector Stencil Computation with Interleaved Outer Product and MLA
problem: Stencil computations are fundamental HPC kernels but suffer from underutilized matrix units, limited instruction-level parallelism, and poor cache hit rates when working sets exceed cache capacity. Existing approaches fail to fully exploit modern matrix-unit capabilities.
motivation: Specialized matrix units (matrix-fused multiply-add, outer-product units) provide substantial computing horsepower, but stencil computations don't map efficiently to these resources. Prior work shows suboptimal utilization due to structural mismatches.
method: HStencil combines three optimizations. Microkernels (small code blocks) run matrix and vector operations together so both processor units work in parallel instead of one sitting idle. Fine-grained instruction scheduling interleaves operations—while one processor unit computes, another fetches data—maximizing parallel execution. Spatial prefetching (pulling nearby data proactively) sustains performance when working sets exceed cache capacity.
key_novelty: The core idea is using matrix and vector compute units together for stencil operations by interleaving outer-product calculations (multiplying vector pairs to build matrix values), with fine-grained scheduling to keep both units constantly busy.
contributions: Microkernel design leveraging both matrix and vector execution units
Interleaved instruction scheduling technique for improved ILP
Spatial prefetch strategy for large working sets
Framework optimizations for different CPU platforms
limitations: Abstract only - no dataset specifics, no breakdown by stencil type or data size, limited architectural coverage details
primary_theme: HPC kernel optimization through hardware feature exploitation
